comments.text: Middle men across every supply chain is the problem with everything being way too expensive. It's the most ridiculous concept in business. Works like this... I have a shitload of start up capital so I go and purchase bulk from the manufacturer because they want to move things fast and at volume. Then I set up a store front with all the vehicles that I bought from the manufacturer, but to turn a profit I must instantly charge the customer more than what I paid for it which Is what the vehicle cost to make plus the profit the manufacturer wanted to make. And then I get greedy so I want to make even more money... I have to add things to the car so justify inflating the price and then I will markup those add-ons to 10x it's value. And then I will partner with a bank so that we can finance through the dealership and squeeze even more money out of the interest payments on the loan... Not to mention all the lies and deceit I can use to hide the truth of how unreliable a car is because I have the mechanics on the payroll that slap shit together just to get it out the door and over warranty before it falls apart, but that's okay because I can pass that cost along to the customer as well.
